page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance built on KVM hypervisor technology. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz with 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs via hyperthreading. The CPU includes 40 MB of L3 cache along with standard AVX, AES, and FMA instruction set support. System memory totals 60 GB, allocating 7.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. Storage and networking specifications include 472 GB of local SSD storage and a 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks highlight strong GPU-driven acceleration paired with modest host CPU throughput. The instance achieves high-ranking results in LLM inference workloads, delivering 316.69 tokens per second for prompt processing and 42.77 tokens per second for text generation on a 7B model. Conversely, CPU-bound synthetic tests show lower performance, including a stress-ng single-core score of 954.2 and a multi-core score of 4765.11. Memory bandwidth tests yield 37.47 GB/sec for uncached reads and 26.02 GB/sec for uncached writes, while PassMark CPU testing scores 6724.43 overall.

The hardware configuration creates a distinct tradeoff between host CPU computing capacity and graphics acceleration capability. While the older CPU architecture limits single-threaded execution speed and lacks AVX-512 support, the onboard NVIDIA P100 GPU provides substantial compute density for parallel mathematical workloads. Bundling 472 GB of local SSD storage allows fast data access for model weights and staging datasets. This instance is best suited for AI inference, medium-scale machine learning model deployment, matrix processing, and graphics workloads.

It includes 472 GB of bundled local SSD storage and a 3 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark data indicates strong hardware-accelerated LLM inference performance, reaching 316.69 tokens per second for 7B model prompt processing and 42.77 tokens per second for text generation. The instance offers resource density for accelerated matrix workloads, local data staging, and medium-scale AI inference, though it is less suitable for high-single-thread CPU intensive tasks.
